question: The period from the decline of the Mauryas to the rise of the Guptas (2nd century BCE to 3rd century CE) is known in Indian history as the _________ period.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Post-Mauryan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The period from the decline of the Mauryas to the rise of the Guptas is referred to as the **Post-Mauryan period**.
 
• This era spanned from the 2nd century BCE to the 3rd century CE.
 
• It was a time of significant political fragmentation and the rise of several regional kingdoms in India.
 
• The Post-Mauryan period saw the growth of new trade routes, the spread of Buddhism and Jainism, and the flourishing of arts and architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maurya Empire**

 
 
• The Maurya Empire, founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE, was one of the largest and most powerful political and military empires in ancient India.
 
• It reached its zenith under Emperor Ashoka, who ruled from 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• Ashoka is renowned for his propagation of Buddhism and his efforts to spread Buddhist values and ethics across his empire and beyond.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Empire**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire was established by Sri Gupta around the early 4th century CE.
 
• It is often referred to as the "Golden Age" of India due to the significant achievements in arts, science, and literature during this period.
 
• Prominent rulers like Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, and Chandragupta II led the empire to its peak.
 
 
 
• **Regional Kingdoms**
 
 
• During the Post-Mauryan period, several regional kingdoms emerged, including the Shungas, Satavahanas, Kushanas, and others.
 
• The Shungas, who succeeded the Mauryas in the Magadha region, were known for their patronage of Brahmanism and the revival of Hindu rituals and practices.
 
• The Satavahanas ruled in the Deccan region and played a crucial role in promoting trade and commerce.
 
• The Kushanas, originating from Central Asia, established a powerful empire in northwestern India and parts of Central Asia, promoting both Buddhism and Hinduism.
 
 
 
• **Cultural and Economic Developments**
 
 
• The Post-Mauryan period witnessed extensive trade routes connecting India with Central Asia, the Middle East, and the Mediterranean world.
 
• Buddhism and Jainism continued to spread, with many monasteries and stupas being built during this time.
 
• Art and architecture flourished, with notable contributions in the form of Gandhara and Mathura school of arts.
